FINAL EXECUTION BLOCK — RECONCILE GITHUB SAFELY, DEPLOY, MIGRATE, TEST, AND CERTIFY ONE BY ONE

The latest report proves that the remaining root blocker is Git divergence:

* Rork/local contains the new IVX security and platform work.
* GitHub `main` contains autonomous commits not present in Rork’s origin.
* Rork auto-sync cannot fast-forward GitHub.
* Production follows GitHub through Render auto-deploy.
* Therefore, production cannot receive the new work until both histories are safely reconciled.
* Do not return another audit or credential inventory.

NON-NEGOTIABLE SAFETY RULES

* Preserve both the Rork/local changes and every GitHub `main` change.
* Do not force-push.
* Do not reset, overwrite, delete, or replace GitHub `main`.
* Do not discard autonomous commits.
* Do not expose credentials.
* Do not claim synchronization, deployment, migration, or certification without executed proof.
* Create a recoverable backup reference before reconciliation.
* Use the existing GitHub/Rork authorization path; do not request credentials unless a real operation returns 401/403.
* If direct `main` updates are protected, create a reconciliation branch and pull request through the existing GitHub integration.

PHASE 1 — CAPTURE AND PROTECT BOTH HISTORIES

1. Fetch the current GitHub `main`.
2. Record the complete 40-character SHA for:

   * Rork/local HEAD
   * Rork origin/base
   * GitHub `main`
   * Production
3. Determine the exact merge base.
4. List commits unique to Rork/local.
5. List commits unique to GitHub `main`.
6. Create a recoverable backup branch/reference for the Rork/local work before changing history.
7. Confirm the backup points to the complete local commit.
8. Do not label a shortened SHA or UUID as a Git SHA.
9. Scan the intended commit set for credentials and local environment files before publishing anything.

Required evidence:

| Reference | Full SHA | Location | Protected |
| --------- | -------- | -------- | --------: |

PHASE 2 — RECONCILE WITHOUT LOSING WORK

Use this preferred method:

1. Create a new reconciliation branch from the current GitHub `main`.
2. Apply the complete Rork/local commit set onto that branch using a normal merge or cherry-pick.
3. Preserve all unrelated GitHub changes.
4. Resolve conflicts file by file using the intended behavior from both sides.
5. Never choose “ours” or “theirs” globally.
6. Inspect every resolved file.
7. Confirm no security middleware, migrations, routes, screens, tests, environment validation, or provider integrations disappeared.
8. Confirm no credentials entered the resulting tree.
9. Run the complete verification suite before updating `main`.
10. Push the reconciliation branch through the existing authorized GitHub connection.
11. If branch protection requires a pull request, open one and report its exact status.
12. If direct merging is authorized and all required checks pass, merge normally without force.
13. Record the resulting full GitHub commit SHA.

The completed tree must contain both:

* All legitimate changes already on GitHub `main`
* All intended Rork/local security, migration, platform, and UI changes

If a real merge conflict cannot be resolved safely, stop only that file and report:

* file path
* conflicting intent from each side
* safe options
* no secret values

Continue all unrelated work.

PHASE 3 — VERIFY THE RECONCILED SOURCE

Run the actual repository commands, installing declared dependencies first:

1. Dependency installation
2. Formatting check
3. Lint
4. Complete backend TypeScript check
5. Complete Expo TypeScript check
6. All backend unit tests
7. All frontend tests
8. Integration tests
9. API tests
10. Diagnostic-security regression tests
11. Database/migration tests
12. Backend production build
13. Expo/web production build
14. Source secret scan
15. Git-diff secret scan
16. Built-client secret scan

Requirements:

* Do not filter out TypeScript error categories.
* Fix ESLint dependency/configuration instead of accepting “ESLint not installed.”
* Diagnose the Expo Watchman/export failure and execute the supported clean build path.
* Do not weaken tests to make them pass.
* The 15 diagnostic-security failures must pass against the reconciled source before live certification.
* Report exact commands, exit codes, and concise real output.

PHASE 4 — PUSH AND PROVE GITHUB SYNCHRONIZATION

After checks pass:

1. Push the reconciled commit through the authorized Rork/GitHub integration.
2. Fetch GitHub `main` again.
3. Verify the intended files can be read from that exact commit.
4. Verify no `.env`, credential file, signing key, bank information, token, or generated secret was committed.
5. Record the full GitHub `main` SHA.
6. Compare the remote tree with the tested reconciliation tree.
7. Certify GitHub synchronization only if they match.

Do not claim success merely because a push command exited zero if GitHub `main` did not advance.

PHASE 5 — OBSERVE THE PROVEN GITHUB-TO-RENDER DEPLOYMENT

GitHub-to-Render auto-deploy is the proven deployment mechanism. Use it instead of blocking on the rejected Render management API credential.

1. Detect the deployment triggered by the reconciled GitHub commit.
2. Record the real deployment ID if accessible.
3. Wait for a terminal deployment state.
4. Inspect available build and startup evidence.
5. Verify production health.
6. Read the full deployed commit SHA from a trustworthy runtime/build endpoint.
7. Compare it exactly with GitHub `main`.
8. If deployment fails, fix the real source/configuration error, create a new reconciled commit, and repeat.
9. Do not call production synchronized unless the complete SHAs match.

The expired Render management key may be reported separately as:

`OPTIONAL MANAGEMENT CHANNEL REJECTED — DEPLOYMENT CONTINUES THROUGH GITHUB AUTO-DEPLOY`

Do not allow it to block a working GitHub-based deployment.

PHASE 6 — VERIFY EVERY SECURITY ENDPOINT INDIVIDUALLY

After deployment, test every sensitive endpoint without authentication:

* `/api/tool/render-status`
* `/api/tool/github-status`
* `/api/ivx/chat-debug`
* `/api/ivx/wire-instructions`
* Every `/api/ivx/deploy-tools/*` route
* `/api/ivx/render-diagnostic`
* `/api/ivx/supabase/tables`
* `/api/ivx/supabase/schema`
* `/api/ivx/supabase/columns`
* `/api/ivx/supabase/rls`
* Every owner AI-auth diagnostic route
* `/api/ivx/verify/env-status`
* `/api/ivx/runtime-variables`
* `/api/ivx/runtime-variables/audit`
* Every other environment, credential, deployment, bank, or diagnostic route registered in `backend/hono.ts`

Each unauthenticated request must return 401, 403, or 404.

Then verify authorized access using the existing owner-auth runtime mechanism without displaying the credential.

For every endpoint report:

| Endpoint | Unauthenticated HTTP | Authorized HTTP | Redacted | Rate-limited | Audited | Status |
| -------- | -------------------: | --------------: | -------: | -----------: | ------: | ------ |

An unauthenticated HTTP 200 containing operational metadata, bank information, repository data, credential state, or internal configuration is a failed security certification.

PHASE 7 — BIND AND CERTIFY CREDENTIALS ONE BY ONE

IVX AI variables and Rork contain the project credential records. For every credential required by the reconciled production code, verify:

`Rork record → IVX AI variable → canonical mapping → deployment binding → active runtime → SDK/header → provider response`

Process separately:

1. Supabase URL
2. Supabase anonymous key
3. Supabase service-role key
4. Supabase database connection
5. IVX AI gateway key
6. AI gateway URL
7. JWT secret
8. Application secret
9. Owner-auth token
10. Internal deployment secret
11. Render service identity
12. Render authorization
13. GitHub repository
14. GitHub authorization only if production code genuinely requires it
15. AWS identity and resources only if the deployed architecture uses them
16. Stripe credentials only if payment custody is enabled
17. Dedicated wire-encryption key
18. Twilio credentials only if notifications are enabled
19. Android signing credentials
20. App Store Connect credentials
21. Google Play service-account credentials
22. Every additional credential referenced by deployed code

For each:

* Check all authorized Rork and IVX locations.
* Determine whether required, optional, obsolete, or provider-managed.
* Compare nonreversible fingerprints where permitted.
* Repair aliases and runtime bindings when an existing value is available.
* Execute the smallest safe provider request.
* Check permissions.
* Check for source, Git, log, and client exposure.
* Never output the value.
* Do not group credentials under a single health result.

Use:

| # | Credential | Required | Rork | IVX AI | Deployment | Runtime | Provider test | Leak test | Status |
| - | ---------- | -------: | ---- | ------ | ---------- | ------- | ------------- | --------- | ------ |

Presence alone is not certification.

PHASE 8 — APPLY BOTH SUPABASE MIGRATIONS

After the reconciled backend is deployed:

1. Use the protected migration runner or existing authorized server-side database connection.
2. Do not expose database credentials.
3. Apply separately:

   * `ivx-real-estate-platform.sql`
   * `ivx-platform-extensions.sql`
4. Make each migration safely repeatable.
5. Record the real migration identifier/result.
6. Verify every expected table through executed queries.
7. Verify indexes, constraints, functions, triggers, and RLS policies.
8. Test unauthenticated, authenticated, owner, and administrative behavior.
9. Verify seeded South Florida pilot-market data.
10. Do not certify migration based on file existence or line count.

If migration execution fails, return the exact sanitized database error and keep the platform state consistent.

PHASE 9 — ACTIVATE AND VERIFY THE AI GATEWAY

1. Locate the existing AI credential in Rork and IVX AI variables.
2. Standardize the server on `IVX_AI_GATEWAY_KEY`.
3. Bind it to the actual production environment.
4. Confirm the correct provider URL and authorization format.
5. Redeploy if required.
6. Execute a minimal provider request.
7. Verify `/health/ai/live`.
8. Confirm client code never receives the key.
9. Do not deploy recurring four-hour probes or SMS alerts unless separately authorized.
10. Report actual provider/model/latency only after execution.

PHASE 10 — CERTIFY POINTS 1–10 INDIVIDUALLY

Certify each point using real live evidence:

1. GitHub synchronization
2. Production synchronization
3. Deployment control
4. Real-estate end-to-end flow
5. Owner system
6. Compliance workflow
7. Payments/escrow software workflow
8. Global core
9. Security
10. South Florida pilot market

Use:

| Point | Source | Full tests | Database | API | UI | Live production | Evidence | Status |
| ----- | -----: | ---------: | -------: | --: | -: | --------------: | -------- | ------ |

Allowed statuses:

* `CERTIFIED — LIVE`
* `CERTIFIED — SOURCE/TEST`
* `BOUND — REDEPLOYMENT REQUIRED`
* `EXTERNAL LICENSED PROVIDER REQUIRED`
* `BLOCKED — EXACT EXECUTED ERROR`
* `FAILED`

Do not mark a point complete merely because source files or SQL exist.

EXTERNAL LICENSED SERVICES

Report software readiness separately for:

* KYC
* escrow
* electronic signatures
* title company
* brokerage
* payment custody

Do not claim legal, regulatory, financial, brokerage, escrow, title, or KYC certification without the appropriate configured and verified licensed provider.

FINAL EVIDENCE-ONLY RESPONSE

Return:

1. Backup branch/reference and full SHA
2. Reconciliation branch and merge method
3. Conflicts and resolutions
4. Files actually changed
5. Commands and exit codes
6. Full test/build results
7. Full reconciled GitHub `main` SHA
8. Render deployment ID/status
9. Full deployed SHA
10. Exact GitHub/deployed SHA comparison
11. One-by-one endpoint certification
12. One-by-one credential certification
13. One-by-one migration certification
14. One-by-one certification of Points 1–10
15. Secret-scan results
16. Exact sanitized blockers
17. Licensed-provider requirements

Do not return another plan. Do not ask whether to continue. Preserve both histories, reconcile safely, test, synchronize, deploy, migrate, verify, and certify every item one by one.
